93100512.extract:
# Tonight (PinkPantheress song)

Tonight is a single by English singer-songwriter PinkPantheress, released on April 4, 2025, through Warner Records UK/Parlophone as the lead single from her 2025 mixtape Fancy That. The dance-pop track runs approximately 2:54 and incorporates an orchestral sample from Panic! at the Disco’s 2008 song Do You Know What I’m Seeing?, resulting in additional songwriting credits for members of the band’s classic lineup. A Bridgerton-inspired music video directed by Charlotte Rutherford was issued the same day. The song entered the UK’s Official Singles Chart Top 100 and spent six weeks on the chart; in the United States it debuted at number 5 on Billboard’s Hot Dance/Pop Songs chart, and it also reached number 12 on Billboard Japan’s Hot Overseas chart. Critics highlighted its hook-filled structure and playful directness, with the track included in Billboard’s “Best Songs of 2025 So Far” list and spotlighted by outlets including Consequence and NME. A set of dance-oriented remixes—featuring JADE, Basement Jaxx, and Joe Goddard—arrived in October 2025 as part of PinkPantheress’s remix project Fancy Some More? 

## Background and release

Following the release of her debut album Heaven Knows (2023), PinkPantheress began previewing new club-focused material in early 2025. On April 4, 2025, she released Tonight as the first single from her second mixtape Fancy That, accompanied by a period-drama-inspired video directed by fashion photographer and director Charlotte Rutherford. Coverage from NME and Rolling Stone emphasized the video’s Regency aesthetic and noted that Tonight marked the beginning of her 2025 release run leading up to Fancy That’s May rollout. In posts highlighted by NME, she teased the video as “Bridgerton mode.” 

The release was supported across major streaming platforms globally on April 4, 2025. Platform listings identify it as a standalone digital single, later included on Fancy That. Qobuz credits frame the project as “A Warner Records UK Release” with PinkPantheress’s recordings licensed to Parlophone. 

## Composition and lyrics

Tonight is a synth-led dance-pop track that blends UK club lineage with catchy, compact hooks. It features a thumping four-on-the-floor pulse and rapid, zippy synths that critics associated with contemporary house, bassline, and broader dance-pop idioms. The song opens with baroque-flavored string figures sampled from Panic! at the Disco’s Do You Know What I’m Seeing? (2008), which lends a wistful, cinematic sheen to the intro before the beat drops. The sample’s use is reflected in the song’s credits, which include Brendon Urie, Ryan Ross, Spencer Smith, and Jon Walker. 

Lyrically, the track is unusually direct and flirty for PinkPantheress, with the chorus pivoting on a blunt proposition (“You want sex with me? … Come talk to me, come on,” as quoted in press coverage), framing the encounter as breathless dancefloor flirtation. Consequence described how the Panic! strings “fold into a lush, club-ready beat” under her featherlight delivery, while Pitchfork characterized the track’s candor as turning “sexual candor into sweetness” amid its brisk rhythmic drive. 

## Music video

The official music video for Tonight premiered on April 4, 2025. Directed by Charlotte Rutherford, it presents a playful Regency/Bridgerton-style house party reimagined through a contemporary pop lens—corsets, pearls, powdered wigs, and lavish manor interiors cut against a modern, DJ-led bash. Rolling Stone and NME noted the Bridgerton inspiration explicitly. The video’s YouTube description lists Rutherford as director and Chris Murdoch as producer. 

## Promotion and live performances

- Digital/visuals: The single arrived with the official video and a lyric video on YouTube on April 4, 2025. 
- Social media and dance trend: A compact dance challenge to the chorus circulated on TikTok and Instagram in the days following release. Billboard reported that PinkPantheress and rapper Doechii posted a branded clip of the dance on April 10, 2025, tagging H&M after an appearance at the retailer’s Los Angeles event. 
- Radio/TV: PinkPantheress performed Tonight in BBC Radio 1’s Live Lounge as part of her October 2025 session. She also made her U.S. late-night TV debut on July 30, 2025, performing a medley of Illegal, Girl Like Me, and Tonight on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon; both Clash and Rolling Stone covered the performance and staging. 

## Critical reception

Coverage of Tonight was broadly favorable, with praise focused on its melody-forward construction, playful lyricism, and sleek club textures.

- Consequence selected it in Staff Picks for Best Songs of the Week upon release, noting the way it folds Panic! at the Disco’s baroque strings into a “lush, club-ready beat,” with her “featherlight vocals” maintaining ease over the bounce. 
- Rolling Stone spotlighted the single and video on release day, commenting on the period-drama concept and quoting the song’s candid chorus lines. 
- In its Fancy That review, Pitchfork highlighted Tonight’s direct hooks and described how the track turns “sexual candor into sweetness” under a fast, pulsing beat. 
- Billboard included Tonight on its “Best Songs of 2025 So Far” list, calling it a “high-stakes dancefloor confessional” driven by thumping bass and frenetic synths, and also featured it in a staff list of the best U.K. & Ireland songs of the year’s first half. 
- NME’s news coverage on release underlined the video’s Bridgerton conceit and the song’s role inaugurating the Fancy That era. A niche review in Stanisland described the track as light, 1990s-inflected dance-pop with comedic simplicity—useful for representing a minority critical view. 

## Commercial performance

- United Kingdom: Tonight entered the UK’s Official Singles Chart Top 100 and spent six consecutive weeks on the chart, covering the period from the week ending April 17, 2025, to May 22, 2025. The Official Charts Company also described it as a Top 40 single in a New Music Friday roundup in May 2025. In October 2025, the track appeared at number 19 on the Official Trending Chart alongside renewed interest in PinkPantheress’s catalog. 
- United States: The track debuted at number 5 on Billboard’s Hot Dance/Pop Songs chart dated April 19, 2025, aided by approximately 3.6 million U.S. streams in its first tracking week, according to Billboard’s Chart Beat column. 
- Japan: On Billboard Japan’s Hot Overseas chart (dated April 28, 2025), Tonight entered at number 12. Billboard Japan also issued a news item announcing the single’s release to the market. 

## Credits and personnel

Credits adapted from Qobuz and platform metadata. 

- PinkPantheress – vocals, songwriter, producer, engineer, programmer, vocal engineer
- Aksel Arvid – songwriter, producer, engineer, programmer
- Count Baldor – songwriter, producer
- Phil – additional production
- Nickie Jon Pabón – mixing engineer
- Colin Leonard – mastering engineer
- Brendon Boyd Urie – songwriter (sample)
- George Ryan Ross – songwriter (sample)
- Spencer James Smith – songwriter (sample)
- Jonathan Jacob Walker – songwriter (sample)
- Label/rights: A Warner Records UK Release; © 2025 PinkPantheress under exclusive license to Parlophone Records Limited; ℗ 2025 Pink Pantheress

## Versions and remixes

- Tonight (original single) – digital single, 1 track (approx. 2:54–2:56 depending on platform) 
- Remixes (October 2025):
 - Tonight (with JADE) – released October 10, 2025 (as part of the remix project Fancy Some More?) 
 - Tonight + Basement Jaxx – listed among remix singles tied to Fancy Some More? 
 - Tonight + Joe Goddard – listed among remix singles tied to Fancy Some More? 

Official Charts reported the Fancy Some More? release for October 10, 2025, and Apple Music and Spotify list Tonight remix singles accordingly. 

## Track listing and formats

- Digital single
 - Tonight – 2:54 (Apple Music time) 

- Digital remixes
 - Tonight (with JADE) – single (duration varies by platform) 
 - Tonight + Basement Jaxx – single 
 - Tonight + Joe Goddard – single 

## Release history

- April 4, 2025 — worldwide digital single release (Apple Music, Spotify) 
- April 4, 2025 — official music video release on YouTube 
- May 2025 — included on the mixtape Fancy That (Warner Records UK/Parlophone) 
- October 10, 2025 — remix releases tied to Fancy Some More? (including Tonight remixes with JADE, Basement Jaxx, Joe Goddard) 

## Notes

- ISRC codes for Tonight were not publicly listed in the consulted platform metadata and IFPI search was not available in the cited materials; credits and rights are documented via Qobuz/TIDAL.
- Cover art creator information for the single was not confirmed via label or official platform notes and is therefore not included.

Pinkpantheress issues new single ‘Tonight’ with ‘Bridgerton’-inspired music video
=================================================================================

Pinkpantheress hosts a party in a grand palace while in full era-appropriate costume

 

By [Daniel Peters](https://www.nme.com/author/daniel-peters)

 

4th April 2025

 

![Image 3](https://www.nme.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/pinkpantheress@2000x1270-696x442.jpg)

PinkPantheress. Credit: Astrida Valigorsky/Getty Images

 

[Pinkpantheress](https://www.nme.com/artists/pinkpantheress) has issued a new single titled ‘Tonight’ with a [_Bridgerton_](https://www.nme.com/series/bridgerton)\-inspired music video.

*   **READ MORE:** [PinkPantheress on the cover: “I don’t care about the beats, I care about the pen”](https://www.nme.com/big-reads/pinkpantheress-cover-interview-2023-take-me-home-ep-3390837)

‘Tonight’ marks the latest music released by the singer-songwriter since 2024’s ‘Turn It Up’, which itself was her sole new material following her [2023 debut album ‘Heaven Knows’](https://www.nme.com/reviews/album/pinkpantheress-heaven-knows-debut-album-review-radar-3533982).

Advertisement

Last January, Pinkpantheress announced that [she is “soooo back” to release new music this year](https://www.nme.com/news/music/pinkpantheress-teases-new-music-for-2025-we-are-soooo-back-3826370) – and ‘Tonight’ is the first. “the Tonight music video is out now honey💋💋 we went bridgerton mode tf”, [she tweeted today](https://x.com/pinkpantheress2/status/1908186494994616735) (April 4).

Its music video, directed by Charlotte Rutherford, shows Pinkpantheress – in a full 19th century-era dress – hosting a party in a grand palace. The night gets more debauched and surreal as it goes on, with a man stepping out of a portrait, its DJ spinning records on gramophones, and a woman flailing amongst unbothered revellers with her hair on fire.

‘Tonight’ leans closer to her synth-powered dance pop sound, as exemplified in ‘Turn It Up’ and ‘Heaven Knows’, instead of the UK garage production of mini-album ‘To Hell With It’. Watch the music video below.

On New Year’s Day, PinkPantheress shared two photos of herself working on her laptop, with music production software visible on the screen – hinting at new material following her brief hiatus.

##### Recommended

“Oh, we are soooo back! #2025” she tweeted, “I missed y’all \[heart emoji\] Thanks for waiting on me \[teary-eyed emoji\].”

In January, Pinkpantheress featured on [‘True Religion’](https://www.nme.com/news/music/shygirl-teams-up-with-isabella-lovestory-and-pinkpantheress-on-new-single-true-religion-3831489), the [Shygirl](https://www.nme.com/artists/Shygirl) single with Isabella Lovestory.

[_NME_ reviewed the London date of her 2024 ‘Capable of Love’ tour](https://www.nme.com/reviews/live/pinkpantheress-live-in-london-setlist-photos-3592949), awarding the show four stars and describing the gig as “a relentless extravaganza” that served as “a launchpad to showcase her newfound confidence on stage.”

Last July, she unfortunately [had to cancel all her remaining dates “to focus on \[her\] physical health and overall wellbeing”.](https://www.nme.com/news/music/pinkpantheress-cancels-remaining-2024-shows-health-reasons-3780260) This meant she would no longer co-headline Field Day 2024 or open for [Coldplay](https://www.nme.com/artists/coldplay) on the Australasian leg of [their ‘Music of the Spheres’ world tour](https://www.nme.com/news/music/coldplay-australia-new-zealand-2024-tour-dates-tickets-3543972).

Advertisement

PinkPantheress also featured on the laidback ‘Snap My Finger’ from [Kaytranada’s third studio album, ‘Timeless’](https://www.nme.com/reviews/album/kaytranada-timeless-review-lyrics-tracklist-3762821) and the remix of [LE SSERAFIM’s viral hit, ‘Crazy’](https://www.nme.com/news/music/le-sserafim-drop-ballroom-inspired-music-video-for-new-single-crazy-3788937) last year. She also had an uncredited feature on ‘Pink XOXO’ from [Camilla Cabello’s latest album, ‘C,XOXO’.](https://www.nme.com/reviews/album/camila-cabello-c-xoxo-album-review-3768433)

[When ‘Heaven Knows’ was released, _NME_ gave the record four stars](https://www.nme.com/reviews/album/pinkpantheress-heaven-knows-debut-album-review-radar-3533982), writing: “Ultimately, what makes ‘Heaven Knows’ such a compelling debut is its ability to create British wistfulness. The emotions and sounds are familiar enough to pull you in, and peculiar enough to make you stay. Heaven knows the boundaries of Pink’s talent to come.”

PinkPantheress Charlie Engham\*

_Bridgerton’s_ Lady Whistledown would have a lot to say about [PinkPantheress](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/pinkpantheress-new-single-turn-it-up-1235027232/)‘ latest single “Tonight,” the video for which finds the innovative musician derailing a regency-era ballroom performance. Directed by Charlotte Rutherford, the clip follows [PinkPantheress](https://www.rollingstone.com/t/pinkpantheress/) and her crew riding up to a mansion on bikes and carriages with plans to make her the most desirable — and chaotic — diamond of the season.

“I leave my bedroom with my posters of you up/I do this all because your my superstar/Ilook at you and I wonder why its so complicated/You’re talking out to a crowd of people who thought you hated/Your friends will tell me you’re too scared of coming up/But tonight, why is it all emotional to me,” PinkPantheress sings on the propulsive dance track. “You want sex with me/Come talk to me/Talk later, that’s why I’m goin’ tonight/You’re hot, on fire, that’s why I’m callin’ tonight/Talk later, that’s why I’m goin’ tonight/Your sex on fire, that’s why I like goin’ tonight.”

“Tonight” will serve as the lead single to PinkPantheress’ forthcoming follow-up to her debut album, 2023’s [_Heaven Knows_.](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-album-reviews/pinkpantheress-heavens-knows-review-1234871713/) “I’m so excited to finally bring out the first single of my new project, I hope everyone has as much fun listening to it as I do,” she shared in a statement.

The single also marks the official return of PinkPantheress after she [cancelled her slate of 2024 appearances](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/pinkpantheress-cancels-2024-shows-health-issues-1235072659/) to focus on her health, including festival performances and an opening slot with Olivia Rodrigo. “It is with the heaviest heart that I sadly have to announce that I will not be able to continue with the rest of my live shows this year in order to focus on my physical health and overall well-being,” she wrote on Instagram at the time. “It appears I have reached a wall which I am struggling to penetrate through … I’m sad to disappoint anyone and can only hope we will be in each other’s company once I return to health.”

_Every week,_ Consequence_’s [Songs of the Week](https://consequence.net/category/cos-exclusive-features/top-song-of-the-week/?app=true) column spotlights the best new tracks from the previous seven days and takes a look at notable releases. Find our new favorites and more on our [Top Songs](https://open.spotify.com/playlist/3JzEbTrAnmxkwoEYLBHw03?si=r6Zwg_mWRr-BSTsM6fkXrA&app=true) playlist, and for other great songs from emerging artists, you can listen to our [New Sounds](https://open.spotify.com/playlist/1HZ829ZASjNvOpFcCTr7mB?si=IfYACwDMQr-Xs0V-I-Qqjw&app=true) playlist. This week, PinkPantheress, S. G. Goodman, The Marías, and many more have unveiled new tracks.  
_

* * *

Staff Picks: March 28th – April 4th 2025
----------------------------------------

**2hollis — “you”**

2hollis is back with his latest collection of songs, _star_, and nearly all of them are floor-filling bangers. One of the most infectious slices of dance pop comes with the Eurotrance-influenced “you,” which moves at such a frenetic pace that it’s surprising Hollis doesn’t let the song fully collapse (like on prior tracks “two bad” and “gold”). What’s so wonderful about “you,” and _star_ as a whole, is the tension between Hollis’ icy distance on the mic and the chaotic rattle of the beats that follow; he’s seemingly a master of this kind of glitched out, paranoid dance music, cathartic at one moment and terrifying the next. While “you” is a cleaner offering overall, it’s yet another great example of 2hollis’ remarkable pop vision. — _Paolo Ragusa_

**By Storm — “Double Trio 2”**

By Storm, the new(ish) outsider hip-hop group formed by the surviving members of Injury Reserve, returned this week with a sequel to their debut single, “Double Trio.” The first track under the name served as a transition between the two projects, and now “Double Trio 2” showcases how rapper Ritchie with a T and producer Parker Corey are continuing to sharpen their artistic vision. The beat is ethereal and intense — an energy that’s matched by the vocal performance — and the bars boldly stare down the experience of grief. It really hits. — _Jonah Krueger_

Advertisement

**Dazy — “Pay No Mind (To the Signs)”**

Dazy has been on a roll: After releasing two EPs toward the end of 2024, the Virginia-based musician is back with a fresh single to further charge up his momentum. A whole lot grimier than the tracks on _IT’S ONLY A SECRET (if you repeat it)_ and _I GET LOST (when i try to get found)_, “Pay No Mind” features James Goodson laying his spacey vocals over a thick layer of distorted fuzz, held firmly in place by mechanical percussion underneath it all. Looking at the way things have been going so far, he’s projected to keep getting better as the year progresses. _— Karan Singh_

**Florist — “Jellyfish”**

It’s officially _Jellywish_ release day, but let’s not forget the last single the dreamy New York band dropped in the days leading up to it. “Jellyfish” is arguably the most upbeat track on the LP, though that hardly says much given Emily Sprague’s gentle vocals guiding the listener through its emotional intricacies. An upbeat, folk-leaning acoustic explores an overthinker’s existential crisis? Yes, please. — _Nicolle Periola_

**The Marías — “Back to Me”**

The Marías’ new single delves into a post-breakup emotional landscape. As lead singer María Zardoya achingly muses, “Just to tell you I’m sorry / Baby, come back to me,” the song captures the paradoxical feeling where, despite knowing it’s over, the immediate desire is simply to alleviate the pain. Born from a spontaneous studio jam session, “Back to Me” features a backdrop of loungey soundscapes, with Zardoya’s beautifully hypnotic vocals transporting listeners to a space of solitude and introspection. _— Aureliano Petrucci_

**Maz — “Circle”**

One of the most compelling tracks from Maz’s debut EP, “Circle” perfectly captures the essence of the Utah-based artist as she sets herself up for success. The final cut on _NPC_‘s tracklist, it pulls together the different styles and approaches she takes across the previous five songs. Springy yet delicate in its execution, the care with which this composition was put together points to a promising career ahead for the singer-songwriter. _— K. Singh_

Advertisement

**PinkPantheress — “Tonight”**

For all her worship of the 2000s, was it really only a matter of time before PinkPantheress expanded her pool of sonic references to include… Panic! at the Disco? “Tonight,” her great new single, takes little of Panic’s pop-punk glam, but it does sample the _Pretty. Odd_ cut “Do You Know What I’m Seeing?” That song’s baroque strings are appropriately blended into PinkPantheress’ lush, club-ready beat, with her feathery vocals sprinkled over like sugar in a latte. No matter the reference point, the samples, or the collaborators, PinkPantheress always makes her mark with effortless cool. — _P. Ragusa_

_Fancy That_
============

[PinkPantheress](https://pitchfork.com/artists/pinkpantheress/)

2025

![Image 3: PinkPantheress Fancy That](https://media.pitchfork.com/photos/680bbcede5608e51e0fe26e3/1:1/w_450%2Cc_limit/PinkPantheress-Fancy-That.jpeg)

8.0

By [Harry Tafoya](https://pitchfork.com/staff/harry-tafoya/)

*   Genre:
    
    Pop/R&B / Electronic
    
*   Label:
    
    Warner
    
*   Reviewed:
    
    May 14, 2025
    

The British singer-producer’s new mixtape is a portal into an alternate universe where UK garage blew up in America and fashion froze in 2006.

Save this story

Save this story

At the beginning of [PinkPantheress](https://pitchfork.com/artists/pinkpantheress/)’ new mixtape, _Fancy That_, the 24-year-old singer and producer has just been hit by the full force of an absurdly potent strain of weed and is starting to feel the world tilt off its axis. “Illegal” swerves straight into peak time, growing more massive and colorful as it crashes through the speakers. If the record’s first seconds are slightly disorienting, it hardly seems to register for the singer—she has to be the most poised stoned person on the planet. Pink’s voice is the cool center of the music’s raging party, beckoning us to follow as she sashays down the rabbit hole. “My name is Pink and I’m really glad to meet you,” she deadpans by way of introduction, “You’re recommended to me by some people.” From here on out she has zero intention of slowing things up.

“Illegal” begins like many of PinkPantheress’ best songs to date: musically busy, charmingly conversational, and locked into a hazy headspace conjured by vintage samples and the once and future sound of drum’n’bass. By now the producer has made a specialty out of using thundering breaks and sparkling melodies to jolt her train of thought and chart a comet’s trail out of her feelings. But unlike her past releases, _Fancy That_ offers no daydreaming detours or moments of zoomed-out introspection. The face she puts on is easy, forthright, and effortlessly cool—she’s arrived at a point of clarity and she’s never been more ready to dance.

Initially, it might have been tempting to assume that, because her songs were so short and went viral on TikTok so easily, her work was too low-stakes and thinly sketched for sustained success. But though “PinkPantheress” began as an anonymous handle, it’s since become an undeniable signature. Her 2023 debut, [_Heaven Knows_](https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/pink-pantheress-heaven-knows/), polished the scrappiness of her early work into tracks that consistently managed to clear the two- and even three-minute mark. While that record yielded some undeniable gems (see the [Joanna Newsom](https://pitchfork.com/artists/3096-joanna-newsom/)\-at-the-rave lament “[Ophelia](https://youtu.be/7zi1Qr_WvHE?si=lAGg64q12R9y2T9z)” or the moony 2-step of “[Mosquito](https://youtu.be/6ztwSTu5B8A?si=BXOK29lm9tMC0yu5)”), her bite-sized approach couldn’t always hold its own at full length. Although it won’t shut down [jokes about her track times](https://x.com/pantheressluv/status/1907527939408699448/), the 20-minute _Fancy That_ is PinkPantheress’ most exciting and fully realized release yet.

_Fancy That_ is a portal into an alternate universe where UK garage successfully crossed the Atlantic and fashion froze in 2006. But apart from the more superficial choices (the cover’s [Lily Allen](https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/9221-alright-still/)–inspired graphic collage, the decision to shoot the music video for “[Stateside](https://pitchfork.com/news/pinkpantheress-shares-new-song-stateside-listen/)” in a JCPenney [parking lot](https://www.instagram.com/p/DI4bCGETiwN/)), Pink’s world-building plays out most vividly in her music. After largely forgoing samples on _Heaven Knows_, _Fancy That_ is an encyclopedia of references that far exceeds stale Y2K cosplay. Subtle clues like the [Panic! at the Disco](https://pitchfork.com/artists/3477-panic-at-the-disco/) strings that segue into “Tonight” or the hilarious, stoned call-and-response with a [Nardo Wick](https://pitchfork.com/artists/nardo-wick/) sample on “Noises” are juxtaposed against some thrilling acts of appropriation. “Illegal” blazes into the mix by isolating and supercharging the synths from [Underworld](https://pitchfork.com/artists/4418-underworld/)’s “[Dark & Long (Dark Train Mix)](https://youtu.be/sHK9usHwxSs?si=bcZRP0F7R7vJvWIK),” while “Girl Like Me” takes a [Basement Jaxx](https://pitchfork.com/artists/300-basement-jaxx/) sample and spins it out into a roaring speed garage banger. British dance music has caught a second life across Gen Z pop; PinkPantheress’ tour through the [hardcore continuum](https://www.thewire.co.uk/in-writing/essays/the-wire-300_simon-reynolds-on-the-hardcore-continuum_introduction) is lived-in and substantial, bringing the legacies of producers like Sunship, Adam F, and MJ Cole into the present while strutting her own glittering new path.

Apart from garage and jungle, PinkPantheress is deeply inspired by emo, an influence heard most clearly in the bleeding-edge intensity of her songwriting. Vulnerable motifs repeat throughout her early music, like the humiliation of being caught emoting in public (“Pain,” “Just for me”), or death as a marker for a relationship’s furthest limits (“Nice to Meet You,” “Ophelia,” “Mosquito”). Though she colored in these feelings with a degree of subtlety, the metaphorical extremes exposed the youthfulness of her perspective. What’s wonderful about _Fancy That_ is how bold and funny it is: This Pink won’t buckle under pressure or spiral when left alone. She takes romantic and everyday disappointment in glorious stride. “Stars” pulls double duty: offering a sympathetic ear to a friend who’s unlucky in love, while soundtracking her own frustration with an unreliable plug. The romantic-sounding “Romeo” is a thoroughly modern kiss-off that delivers the fatal blow with a couplet as withering as it is inclusive: “You can fall in love with boys and girls and in between/So I promise that you shouldn’t waste your time on all of me.”

Pink is equally forthright about sex and desire. It’s thrilling to hear her put Abercrombie & Fitch hotties through their paces on “Stateside,” [paying her respects](https://youtu.be/Ic5vxw3eijY?si=WS5UgseLwcYMXdJV) to [Estelle](https://pitchfork.com/artists/5765-estelle/) and putting a sexy spin on the “[special relationship](https://www.instituteforgovernment.org.uk/explainer/us-uk-special-relationship)” all in one go. But “Tonight” is even more impressive: a song-length come-on where the fast-paced thump mirrors a dawning sense of romantic urgency. Even if she plays the directness of a hook like “You want sex with me?/Come talk to me” for giggles, there’s an overriding sweetness that kicks the song into a higher level of feeling. She occupies the space between the bouncing, full-bodied bassline and plaintive keyboards with a plainly stated want that would be unthinkable on her introverted early releases. Having come so fully into her own, PinkPantheress still aspires to reach out to you.

10.title: Dance Moves: Skrillex, 2hollis, PinkPantheress & More Debut on Dance Charts With New Projects
10.description: Skrillex, 2hollis, PinkPantheress and more debut on Billboard's dance charts with their new projects.
10.content:
[Skip to main content](https://www.billboard.com/music/chart-beat/skrillex-2hollis-pinkpantheress-new-projects-dance-charts-1235947832/#pagetop)[](https://www.billboard.com/music/chart-beat/skrillex-2hollis-pinkpantheress-new-projects-dance-charts-1235947832/)

Dance Moves: Skrillex, 2hollis, PinkPantheress & More Debut on Dance Charts With New Projects
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Check out the latest action across _Billboard_'s dance charts.

![Image 1: Skrillex](https://www.billboard.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/Skrillex-cr-NAKEESHA-2025-press-billboard-1548.jpg?w=942&h=628&crop=1)

Skrillex NAKEESHA

_[Billboard](https://www.billboard.com/t/billboard/)_’s [Dance](https://www.billboard.com/t/dance/) Moves roundup serves as a guide to the biggest movers and shakers across _Billboard_’s many dance charts — new No. 1s, new top 10s, first-timers and more.

See latest videos, charts and news

This week on charts dated April 19, Skrillex, 2hollis, PinkPantheress and others achieve new feats. Check out key movers below.

Skrillex
--------

The influential DJ-producer dropped his fourth studio album, _F*CK U SKRILLEX YOU THINK UR ANDY WARHOL BUT UR NOT!! <3_, on April 1 amid _Billboard_‘s Friday-Thursday (March 28-April 3) chart tracking week. The 34-cut set debuted at No. 4 on Top Dance Albums and No. 124 on the [Billboard 200](https://www.billboard.com/charts/billboard-200/) on the April 12-dated charts after just three days of tracking with 11,000 equivalent album units earned, according to Luminate. Following its first full week of tracking (April 4-10, for the latest charts dated April 19), the set rises to No. 3 on Top Dance Albums and No. 69 on the Billboard 200 with 14,000 units.

The project is Skrillex’s eighth career entry on Top Dance Albums and seventh on the Billboard 200. Here’s a look at his history on the former:

_Peak Position, Title, Peak Date:_

*   No. 1 (10 weeks), _Bangarang_, Feb. 11, 2012
*   No. 1 (five weeks), _Recess_, April 5, 2014
*   No. 1 (three weeks), _Skrillex and Diplo Present Jack Ü_, March 14, 2015
*   No. 2, _Quest for Fire_, March 4, 2023
*   No. 3, _F*CK U SKRILLEX YOU THINK UR ANDY WARHOL BUT UR NOT!! <3,_ April 19, 2025
*   No. 3, _Scary Monsters and Nice Sprites,_ Sept 10, 2011
*   No. 5, _More Monsters and Sprites_, July 9, 2011
*   No. 6, _Don’t Get Too Close_, March 4, 2023

Skrillex concurrently debuts five tracks from the new album on Hot Dance/Electronic Songs: “Voltage” (No. 11); “Spitfire,” with HAWAII SLIM (No. 18); “Recovery,” with Space Laces (No. 21); “Andy” (No. 22); and “While You Were Sleeping VIP,” with Virtual Riot and Nakeesha (No. 25). He has charted 69 total entries on the chart, fourth-best after only David Guetta (94), Marshmello (75) and Kygo (70).

Before _Billboard_ launched Hot Dance/Electronic Songs on Jan. 26, 2013, Skrillex logged four songs on the [Billboard Hot 100](https://www.billboard.com/charts/hot-100/): “First of the Year (Equinox)” (No. 85 peak in January 2012); “Scary Monsters and Nice Sprites” (No. 69, 2012); “Kyoto,” featuring Sirah (No. 74, 2012); and “Bangarang” (No. 72, 2012). “Bangarang” also reached No. 19 on Dance/Mix Show Airplay. (He has added six Hot 100 entries since.)

Thanks to their guest appearances, HAWAII SLIM and Nakeesha both score their first _Billboard_ chart hits. Space Laces tallies his fourth entry on Hot Dance/Electronic Songs, after “Destroid 1 Raise Your Fist,” with Excision and Downlink (No. 50 peak in 2013), and two collaborations with Marshmello in 2024: “Conquer” and “Rave Repeater” (Nos. 25 and 36, respectively). Virtual Riot makes his first _Billboard_ chart visit in nine years, since his EP _Chemistry_ reached No. 20 on Top Dance Albums in 2016.

_F*CK U SKRILLEX_ is comprised of [34 tracks](https://www.billboard.com/lists/skrillex-album-review-fck-u-skrillex-andy-warhol-tracks-ranked/), 11 of which are less than one minute in length. The opening track notes that the album is best listened to from start to finish, as it plays at 46 minutes long as a continuous mix. It has more than two dozen collaborators, including Bibi Bourelly, Boys Noize, Dylan Brady of 100 gecs, G Jones, Jónsi of Sigur Rós and Wuki.

2hollis
-------

The Los Angeles-based artist debuts on _Billboard_’s album charts for the first time with his new LP, _Star_. Released April 4 on Interscope Records as his major-label debut, the set arrives at No. 11 on Top Dance Albums (5,000 units). 2hollis had appeared on _Billboard_’s charts once before this week: on Oct. 19, 2024, “Gold” (which is included on _Star_) debuted and peaked at No. 31 on Hot Dance/Electronic Songs. He also reached No. 26 on the now-defunct TikTok Billboard Top 50 in November with “Jeans.”

2hollis served as the opening act for Ken Carson’s The Chaos Tour last year. He performed at Coachella last weekend and is slated to perform at Bonnaroo, Lollapalooza Chicago and Outside Lands.

PinkPantheress
--------------

The multifaceted singer-songwriter-producer returns to _Billboard_’s charts with her new single “Tonight.” Released April 4 via Parlophone/Warner Records, the song debuts at No. 5 on Hot Dance/Pop Songs with 3.6 million U.S. streams in its first week. “Tonight” is the lead single off her upcoming second mixtape, _Fancy That_, due May 9.

PinkPantheress previously charted two tracks on Hot Dance/Electronic Songs: “Way Back” with Skrillex and Trippie Redd reached No. 13 in January 2023, and Kaytranada’s “Snap My Finger” featuring PinkPantheress hit No. 40 last June. Her breakthrough collaboration with Ice Spice, “Boy’s a Liar, Pt. 2,” climbed to No. 3 on the Hot 100 in March 2023 and also spent a week at No. 1 on the Streaming Songs chart.

Rudimental & Khalid
-------------------

Rudimental and Khalid’s new collaboration, “All I Know,” debuts at No. 17 on Hot Dance/Electronic Songs thanks almost entirely to its streaming sum: 958,000 in its first week, after it arrived April 4 via Rudimental/Room Two Recordings. The song earns British trio Rudimental its eighth entry on Hot Dance/Electronic Songs, and first since “Waterslides,” with Tiësto and Absolutely, last year. Notably, Rudimental appeared on the inaugural Hot Dance/Electronic Songs chart in 2013 with “Feel the Love,” featuring John Newman. “All I Know” earns Khalid his seventh entry on the chart, and first since “The Hard Way,” with Pnau, in 2023.

Layton Giordani, Linney & Sarah de Warren
-----------------------------------------

All three artists debut at No. 34 on _Billboard_’s Dance/Mix Show Airplay chart with their collaboration “Act of God.” Layton Giordani and Sarah de Warren claim their first-ever _Billboard_ chart appearances and Linney her second, after her team-up with Tritonal, “Electric Kids,” in 2020 (No. 32 peak on Dance/Mix Show Airplay). Released Jan. 24 on Experts Only, “Act of God” arrives thanks to a 70% increase in plays (among 24/7 dance reporters and pop stations’ mix show hours).

Giordani hails from New York City, with his catalog centered on techno [music](https://www.billboard.com/t/music/). He has released two full-length albums: _Where It Begins_ in 2017, and _New Generation_ in 2020. He has collaborated with Anyma, deadmau5, Dom Dolla and Oliver Heldens, among others.

Singer-songwriters Linney and de Warren have both lent their voices to other dance/electronic tracks. Linney has been releasing music for more than a decade and dropped her latest EP, _We Dance_ (via Helix Records), in September. Warren’s catalog also stretches back that long and includes collaborations with the likes of Hardwell, HI-LO and Weird Genius.

**PinkPantheress** played an incredible medley on American TV overnight (July 30th).

The UK star is having an incredible year, with her album ‘Fancy That’ bowling over critics with its inventive pop blend. PinkPantheress offers audio effervescence, and the release framed her undoubted strengths.

In our review, **[Clash wrote:](https://www.clashmusic.com/reviews/pinkpantheress-fancy-that/)**

_Sounds of the UK run through every track — garage, jungle, indie-dance, Brit girlie pop — but this time, it feels more curated. The Sugababes interpolation on ‘Nice to Know You’ reflects her sharpened instincts, repurposing melodies to bridge eras and connect generations. No features, no distractions. Just her, telling stories and building a new soundscape out of the one that raised her._

Making her debut on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, PinkPantheress opted for a medley of some of her most important tracks. ‘Illegal’, ‘Girl Like Me’, and ‘Tonight’ segued into one another, with PinkPantheress backed by an ebullient DJ.

The backing dancers were dressed in 2005 fashions, and their intricate steps perfectly framed PinkPantheress’ performance.

It’s a set that felt like a real moment – even down to the bloody pre-show skit, in which PinkPantheress accidentally **[tore off Jimmy Fallon’s arm…](https://x.com/capableofluv/status/1950742804533002426)**

A superstar, honestly. Tap in below.

PinkPantheress performs on ‘The Tonight Show.’ Todd Owyoung/NBC via Getty Image

[PinkPantheress](https://www.rollingstone.com/t/pinkpantheress/) made her TV debut last night, appearing on _[The Tonight Show](https://www.rollingstone.com/t/the-tonight-show/)_ to perform a dance-ready medley of three of her songs. With the help of a DJ and a group of backup dancers, the British musician showcased a lively mash-up of “Illegal,” “Girl Like Me,” and “Tonight.”

All three songs come off PinkPantheress’ most recent mixtape, [_Fancy That_](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/pinkpantheress-track-list-mixtape-fancy-that-1235311655/), which arrived on May 9. It marked her first major release in two years, following her 2023 debut album, _[Heaven Knows](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-album-reviews/pinkpantheress-heavens-knows-review-1234871713/)_. The 10-track mixtape notably sampled Panic! at the Disco’s song “Do You Know What I’m Seeing?” on “Tonight.”

“Sampling is funny because everyone has their opinions about it. Some people think it’s stealing or unoriginal, which is something I dealt with a lot when I was starting,” the musician told _[MixMag](https://mixmag.net/feature/pinkpantheress-cover-feature-interview-2025)_. “But for me sampling is my way of sharing a love for something and reinterpreting it. I would only sample something I love, I would never sample something for the thought of it having nostalgia-bait or whatever reason. I do it because I want to reinterpret something I love to different audiences.”

PinkPantheress will embark on a short tour, [An Evening With PinkPantheress](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/pinkpantheress-fancy-that-residency-tour-1235365822/), in North America this fall. The live event will make nine stops across six cities: The tour will begin in October with two back-to-back shows at Kings Theatre in Brooklyn, followed by another pair of shows at Toronto’s Massey Hall. PinkPantheress will stop in Chicago for a night at Byline Bank Aragon Ballroom before heading to Los Angeles for two nights at the Wiltern. The live run will conclude with shows in San Francisco and Oakland in November.

The singer is getting back into the swing of touring after [canceling](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/pinkpantheress-cancels-2024-shows-health-issues-1235072659/) all of her scheduled 2024 appearances this past August. “I was full up. There was something that I needed to address, and so I had to leave,” the musician told [Zane Lowe on Apple Music 1](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/pinkpantheress-canceled-shows-zane-lowe-1235333842/) earlier this year. “And I did that for my own good. And obviously it was a very sad moment for people that wanted to see me but couldn’t see me. But obviously, what goes around comes around, and I’ll be back again.”

PinkPantheress announces remix project Fancy Some More? featuring JADE, Sugababes and Kylie Minogue
===================================================================================================

Bladee, Ravyn Lenae, Basement Jaxx and Zara Larsson also feature on the star-studded project.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

![Image 10: PinkPantheress Fancy Some More](https://www.officialcharts.com/sites/default/files/styles/content_column_mobile/public/2025-10/Pink%20Pantheress%20Fancy%20Some%20More.jpg?itok=0qTSbXcX)

* * *

[PinkPantheress](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/59943/pinkpantheress/) has announced Fancy Some More?, a remix project featuring reimagined versions of tracks from her Fancy That mixtape.

The genre-fusing singer, songwriter and producer has assembled quite a cast list for the remix project, with JADE, Sugababes, Kylie Minogue, Rachel Chinouriri and Aniita all making appearances.

In total, there are 22 new versions of Fancy That tracks, including collabs with Bladee, Ravyn Lenae, Basement Jaxx, Nia Archives and Zara Larsson. The remix project is set for release this Friday (October 10).

PinkPantheress said in a press release: "With this remix project, Fancy Some More, I wanted to explore how the songs can live in different worlds while still holding onto the emotion of the original.

"Hearing other artists reimagine it has been so inspiring. Each remix brings a new energy and texture, while still keeping the heart of the track intact. It’s been so exciting to see Fancy That take on these new, international lives and global perspectives."

### MORE: [See where every PinkPantheress release has charted in the UK](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/59943/pinkpantheress/)

PinkPantheress dropped her Fancy That mixtape in May and saw it debut at Number 3 on the Official Albums Chart – her highest placing to date. It's since been [nominated for this year's Mercury Music Prize](https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/mercury-prize-albums-year-nominees-2025-list/), which will be awarded next Thursday (October 16).

New Music Friday: Arcade Fire, Sleep Token, PinkPantheress, Stormzy and more
============================================================================

New Music Friday - this week's biggest new song, album and DVD releases, all in one place
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

![Image 10: New Music Friday Song Single Album Releases List May 9th 2025](https://www.officialcharts.com/sites/default/files/styles/content_column_mobile/public/2025-05/New%20Music%20Friday%20Song%20Single%20Album%20Releases%20List%20May%209th%202025.jpg?itok=EMYGdXxA)

By Nick Levine | 08 May 2025

share:[Share on Facebook![Image 11: Share on Facebook](blob:https://www.officialcharts.com/40591d706d1c3f2a82207b6b11a09bb6)](javascript:void\(0\))[Share on Twitter![Image 12: Share on Twitter](blob:https://www.officialcharts.com/5319b25504889176c307a6802ff90863)](javascript:void\(0\))[Share on WhatsApp![Image 13: Share on WhatsApp](blob:https://www.officialcharts.com/3dbabd8b9a7cb58cdee80998d3a65943)](javascript:void\(0\))[Share on LinkedIn![Image 14: Share on LinkedIn](blob:https://www.officialcharts.com/9a30dee02fa1cc5b025bf509a34a8a06)](javascript:void\(0\))[Share on Reddit![Image 15: Share on Reddit](blob:https://www.officialcharts.com/b9248b221d651bf490de48c5b78c8ba2)](javascript:void\(0\))[Share via Email![Image 16: Share via email](blob:https://www.officialcharts.com/87c9a2b43250ffff6987a6c4b94171c6)](javascript:void\(0\))

* * *

Welcome to [New Music Friday](https://www.officialcharts.com/new-releases/), your one place to discover the biggest new song, album and DVD releases.

Let's start with albums this week, because there are some _very_ hotly anticipated long-players dropping.

Canadian rock behemoths [Arcade Fire](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/16748/arcade-fire/) are back with their seventh studio album, Pink Elephant, which teams them with U2 and Bob Dylan producer Daniel Lanois. They'll be aiming for their fifth Number 1 on the Official Albums Chart, but they face some stiff competition.

Very much in contention are enigmatic metal band [Sleep Token](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/56767/sleep-token/), who scored a major Official Charts breakthrough in April when [Caramel](https://www.officialcharts.com/songs/sleep-token-caramel/) became their first Top 10 single.

Their last album Take Me to Eden peaked at Number 3 in 2023. Can they chart even higher with new album Even in Arcadia?

![Image 17: Sleep Token band who are members without masks](https://www.officialcharts.com/sites/default/files/styles/content_column_mobile/public/2025-04/Sleep%20Token%20band%20who%20are%20without%20mask%20members%20Caramel%20song%20Emergence.jpg?itok=xFXPAtcz)

Meanwhile, consistently vibey singer-songwriter-producer [PinkPantheress](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/59943/pinkpantheress/) is dropping a new mixtape, Fancy That, which is already home to the Top 40 single Tonight.

And Brighton indie crew [The Kooks](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/17090/kooks/) are adding to their discography this week with a seventh studio set, Never/Know. It's their follow-up to 2022's 10 Tracks to Echo in the Dark, which peaked at Number 32.

Reading alt-rockers [The Amazons](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/50105/amazons/) are back, too, with their fifth studio album 21st Century Fiction. Can they beat the Number 5 peak of their last album, 2022's How Will I Know if Heaven Will Find Me?

Other notable new albums come from Mark Pritchard & Thom Yorke (Tall Tales), Maren Morris (Dreamsicle) and Kali Uchis (Sincerely,).

![Image 18: stormzy-press-1100.jpg](https://www.officialcharts.com/sites/default/files/styles/content_column_mobile/public/legacy_images/media/654364/stormzy-press-1100.jpg?itok=KRTHYc0J)

Now, let's crack on with this week's singles.

The inimitable [Stormzy](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/32902/stormzy/) drops a double release with swaggering freestyle banger SORRY RACH! and Hold Me Down; both showing off his formidable wordplay skills. Could it become his 16th Top 10 single – or even his fifth Number 1?

Ad

Meanwhile, [Miley Cyrus](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/5138/miley-cyrus/) is continuing to preview her upcoming visual anthem Something Beautiful; she'll be hoping that new single More to Lose becomes the 27th UK Top 40 hit if her prolific career.

Meanwhile, [Tyla](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/tyla/) returns with Bliss, the first single from her forthcoming second album, and 5 Seconds of Summer's Calum Hood shares Call Me When You Know Better, another song from his upconing solo album Order Chaos Order.

Elsewhere, rising singer-songwriter Eden Hunter serves up Knock Me Out. On her inspiration behind the track, Eden says: "\[It's my love letter to the city, to Hollywood, to the showgirls who stay true, to those who dragged me from the pits and told me I’m not the victim anymore, to myself for trusting in the magic of delusion…always."

Belong Together hitmaker [Mark Ambor](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/mark-ambor/) is back, too, with new single Who Knows. As is massively talented multi-hyphenate Tim Minchin, who shares pithy new single The Song of the Masochist.

![Image 19: mark ambor artist hub belong together official charts](https://www.officialcharts.com/sites/default/files/styles/content_column_mobile/public/2024-04/mark%20ambor%20hub.jpg?itok=XUMvFTNY)

It's a packed week for collabs, too. Halsey and Amy Lee team up for Hand That Feeds; Calvin Harris and Clementine Douglas join forces for Blessings; and Avril Lavigne and Simple Plan unite to give us Young & Dumb.

Oh, and [Take That](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/31006/take-that/) fans will be excited to hear a new remix of Hanging Onto Your Love, a deep cut from the band's chart-topping 1995 album Nobody Else. It's been given a club-friendly remix by none other than band member Howard Donald.

Official Trending Chart: Lady Gaga, Gunna, Sienna Spiro and more
================================================================

Your insight into the future hits you need to get to know on the Official Singles Chart
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

![Image 10: Trending Charts 14-10-25](https://www.officialcharts.com/sites/default/files/styles/content_column_mobile/public/2025-10/Trending%20Charts%2014-10-25.jpg?itok=vf4jcpPs)

* * *

With her Mayhem Ball Tour in full flow, [Lady Gaga](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/5334/lady-gaga/) tops the UK's Official Trending Chart this week with her latest single, [The Dead Dance](https://www.officialcharts.com/songs/lady-gaga-the-dead-dance/). The track is also set to re-enter the Top 20 on the Official Singles Chart this Friday.

Following the announcement that [Gunna](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/54444/gunna/) will be heading on tour in 2026 including a night at the O2 London which sold out last night, his hit [wgft](https://www.officialcharts.com/songs/gunna-burna-boy-wgft/) featuring [Burna Boy](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/29059/burna-boy/) catapults to Number 2. Moreover, the single is on course to attain its highest ever position on the Singles Chart, tracking for Number 24.

A rising star in the making, [Sienna Spiro](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/sienna-spiro/) makes the Top 3 on the Trending Chart with her newest offering, [Die On This Hill](https://www.officialcharts.com/songs/sienna-spiro-die-on-this-hill/). The jazz-inspired singer/songwriter whose singing videos have gone viral on TikTok also finds her other release [You Stole The Show](https://www.officialcharts.com/songs/sienna-spiro-you-stole-the-show/) (18) in the trending Top 20, marking a strong week of momentum for the young Brit.

[Tkandz and CXSPER](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/tkandzcxsper/) also see their viral hit [NOW OR NEVER](https://www.officialcharts.com/songs/tkandzcxsper-now-or-never/) making strong moves, hitting Number 4 this week.

And rounding off the Top 5 is Merseyside rapper [EsDeeKid](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/esdeekid/) featuring [Rico Ace](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/rico-aceesdeekid/) with [Phantom](https://www.officialcharts.com/songs/rico-aceesdeekid-phantom/). The track, which has has been gaining serious attention, is also on course to jump six this week on the main Official Singles Chart.

After Fancy Some More? a remix album of [PinkPantheress](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/59943/pinkpantheress/)' [Fancy That](https://www.officialcharts.com/albums/pinkpantheress-fancy-that/) was released this week, the track [Stateside](https://www.officialcharts.com/songs/pinkpantheress-stateside/) from the original album has gained a sudden resurgence in popularity, sitting at Number 8 on the Trending Chart. The Mercury nominated artist also finds [Tonight](https://www.officialcharts.com/songs/pinkpantheress-tonight/) breaking the Top 20 (19).

Other new entries in the Trending Chart this week sees [Skepta](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/5188/skepta/) with Finessekid on [Sirens (From Ireland)](https://www.officialcharts.com/songs/skeptafinessekid-sirens-from-ireland/) (11), [A Boogie Wit Da Hoodie](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/52384/a-boogie-wit-da-hoodie/) with [Part of Me](https://www.officialcharts.com/songs/a-boogie-wit-da-hoodie-part-of-me/) (12), [David Guetta](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/816/david-guetta/)'s link up featuring [Teddy Swims](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/60257/teddy-swims/) and [Tones & I](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/56772/tones-and-i/) on [Gone Gone Gone](https://www.officialcharts.com/songs/guettateddy-swimstones-i-gone-gone-gone/) (15), and finally [Fred again..](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/57051/fred-again/) with [Danny Brown](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/26770/danny-brown/) on [OGdub](https://www.officialcharts.com/songs/fred-againdanny-brown-ogdub/) (16).

_The Official Trending Chart is based on the first four sales days of each chart week (that's Friday to Monday) and ranks those songs showing week-on-week growth on the Official Top 100 Singles Chart, limited to two tracks per artist._
